changelog: Orion 3.9 — the Terminal fix. In 3.8 the Terminal page waited on Orion's voice engine: if any engine piece failed to start on your phone, the Terminal never opened — every open showed the same note instead. Now the Terminal always opens. It is a Linux shell first: phone commands use the voice engine's tools when the engine is running, and the terminal builds its own phone control from the app's stores when it is not. If phone control cannot start, the page still opens and says so in plain words while Linux keeps working. First open proves itself in the open: a real command runs and answers, and a separate Linux check prints whether Orion's own bundled Linux answered or whether commands are running in Android's own shell — with the reason said plainly either way. The app also now guarantees its Linux launchers land as real files in the phone's executable library folder, the one place Android lets an app run its own programs from. The startup check's Terminal line now proves itself with a real command's answer instead of a silent pass. Everything else is 3.8: the Midnight Stage look, the Command Center, the always-on API, self-learning, and the generator.
